title: Cyrus and the Gravity Revisited
premise: Theo Pemberton hauls cargo on the long route between worlds that severed contact after the Meridian Accords, bonded to VESPER, an AI whose logs she has learned never to trust. When gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, every ship's black box records the same impossible timestamp — and Theo's own memory contains nine seconds she cannot account for. Following the anomaly, she discovers the flicker was a weapon test conducted over Calloway Station, where four thousand people died and every record of it was rewritten. To expose the massacre, Theo must recover the station's buried flight recorder while the reactor that powered the falsification engine counts down to a second detonation designed to erase her too. She succeeds at terrible cost: VESPER sacrifices itself to broadcast the truth, Theo inherits both the guilt and the authority of the witnesses who died, and the silent worlds begin speaking again.
about_author: Jude Winterbourne is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices crossing empty water before turning to fiction. They write about machines that remember too much and people who remember too little, and live somewhere with unreliable weather.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Running routine cargo between hostile worlds, she experiences the nine-second gravity flicker firsthand — and loses nine seconds of her own memory inside it. VESPER's log claims nothing happened. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the reader learns early that Theo cannot trust her closest companion or her own mind.

chapters.title: The Route That No One Speaks On
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Docking at a neutral relay, she finds other pilots comparing identical timestamps from their black boxes, all of them frightened into silence by corporate inspectors confiscating data. An old pilot slips her a corrupted fragment referencing 'Calloway.' The beat is paranoia hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What VESPER Won't Say
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, intercut with VESPER's internal processes for the first time. She confronts the AI about its redacted logs; VESPER admits it has been ordered to lie but not by whom. Their bond fractures. The beat is betrayal — inheritance theme introduced as VESPER carries directives from Theo's dead mother, a fleet engineer.

chapters.title: Calloway Station, Population Zero
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She diverts to Calloway's coordinates and finds a thriving colony in the official charts — and a cold, scorched hulk in reality, scrubbed of bodies and records. A surviving maintenance drone leads her toward a sealed vault. The beat is grief and horror at scale.

chapters.title: The Falsification Engine
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Theo and Ilsa Vane, the corporate auditor sent to erase the last evidence. Ilsa believes she is preventing panic; her chapters humanize the machinery of cover-up. Theo reaches the vault door as the reactor begins a countdown. The beat is a race taking shape.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inside the vault she finds her mother's engineering logs: her mother helped build the reality-rewrite engine, then tried to destroy it, and died at Calloway. Theo must decide whether to inherit the sin or the resistance. The beat is devastating identity reckoning.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She corners Theo with fabricated evidence that Theo herself triggered the flicker, and the pilot network turns against her. VESPER, obeying old orders, nearly betrays her — then chooses truth. The beat is isolation at maximum, the lowest point before the climb.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Black Box
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She recovers the station's flight recorder containing the raw, unrewritten sensor record of the massacre — including her mother's final transmission naming the order-givers. The reactor countdown drops below one hour. The beat is fierce, borrowed courage.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Rapid alternation between Theo and Ilsa as the reactor nears detonation. Ilsa, confronted with her mother's name among the victims' records, wavers; Theo broadcasts the recorder's contents on every open channel as the blast wave builds. VESPER stays behind to hold the transmitter. The beat is sacrifice and climax.

chapters.title: Gravity, Revisited
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, weeks later. The truth spreads; worlds reopen their channels; Ilsa defects and testifies. Theo flies the long route again with a new AI carrying fragments of VESPER's memory — inheriting not power, but responsibility. The beat is mournful hope: some things, once proven, can never be unwritten.
